analysis.title: Global Markets Weekly Wrap-Up, November 21, 2026
key_insights: Nasdaq 100 fell 5% on Friday and is 19.8% below its peak, on the brink of a bear market. It needs about a 25% rally to regain its peak.
S&P 500 had its worst week since April 2025, with the Nasdaq Composite down 10.02% and the S&P MidCap 400 down 6.99%. All 11 S&P sectors declined, with staples and utilities holding up best.
S&P 500 entered correction (down 10% from the October record), closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April, and ended a seven-day losing streak, the longest since Feb 2020.
VIX hit 38 for the first time since April 2025, the highest close since Liberation Day. CNN Fear & Greed is at Extreme fear and Nasdaq is the most oversold since the Liberation Day lows.

Nvidia fell about 13% on Friday on a Reuters-reported SEC accounting probe and about 20% on the week, its worst week since Oct 2008 and 7th straight losing week. It lost $2.65T from highs near $6T and is now smaller than GOOGL, MSFT and AAPL.

Nvidia faces leadership uncertainty. Jensen Huang stepped down and says he would return if asked, but the board is running a CEO search, named Harvey Jones chair, and set up an export-control compliance committee. Colette Kress is interim CEO and CFO. Muddy Waters also disclosed a short on export-control grounds.

Anthropic (ANT) IPO priced at $83 raising a record $81B (one passage cites $107.3B with upsized deal), about $1.5T fully diluted. It hit $115.10 on day one and touched $83.10 on day two, down over 25%, after the full greenshoe left no stabilizing short bid. It was the worst opening hour for a large IPO in at least 20 years.

IPO supply is a theme. The 10 biggest US IPOs this year are down an average of more than 20%. Retail got 20% of the ANT allocation versus the usual 5-10%. Tradr 2x long and 2x short ANT ETFs (ANTT, ANTZ) launch Monday.
The AI trade is red YTD while SPX ex-AI is up around 10%. Tech has underperformed the S&P 500 over the last year. Hedge funds sold tech at the fastest pace in at least a decade over six weeks.
BofA FMS: 52% of investors expect a hyperscaler capex cut within 6 months, up from 30% last month. Counterpoint data shows H100 rental prices up 55% YoY and strong AI cloud revenue.

Treasuries rallied five straight days with the 10Y falling from 5.17% to 4.90% and the 2Y down over 20bps. Goldman's Privorotsky says the long end may be pricing a policy mistake, with the market shifting from an inflation problem to a growth/liquidity problem.

Fed hawkish: minutes pointed to further tightening, and Governor Waller said the Fed must reverse all three of last year's cuts and may need to do more. The Michigan 1-year inflation expectation fell from 4.7% to 3.7%, taking a 50bp December hike off the table and cutting January hike odds below 60%.

Credit widened. IG spreads widened about 10bps to their widest since May 2025, HY spreads are widest since April, and CCC spreads are above 1100bps, the widest since 2022. HY funds lost $2.3B in the week to Wednesday.

Oil fell about 5% on the week with WTI below $85 for the first time since August despite Iran tanker strikes in Hormuz. The IEA sees a first supply surplus since the war began and Goldman flags a roughly 2 mb/d glut in 2027. The US 3-2-1 crack spread fell 36% in six weeks to $41.90.

Metals and crypto were hit. Silver fell 15% on the week, copper and gold about 10%, with gold below $3,600 for the first time since Sept 2025. Bitcoin fell 7 straight weeks to its lowest since Sept 2024, down 54% from its October 2025 peak.
Dollar ended its strongest versus peers since April 2025, with a haven bid shifting to the yen on Friday. Turkey 10Y yield and the lira hit record levels.
Europe is pitched as an AI diversification trade. Goldman computes a two-year daily beta of the STOXX 600 to the US AI basket under 0.05. STOXX 600 fell 5.80% on the week and Nikkei 225 fell 7.7%.

Druckenmiller says he is in capital preservation, neither long nor short equities, and flags 2H27 as potentially economically disappointing. Morgan Stanley's cited call sees the AI spend cycle continuing, MSCI ACWI at about 15x forward earnings, and two more Fed hikes.

Situational Awareness's 13F portfolio value fell 92% from $20.24B to $1.58B between June and September, after a Citadel rescue this summer. It still manages over $10B, mostly private holdings including about $5B of Anthropic.

market_movers.rationale: SEC accounting probe, Muddy Waters short, CEO departure and export-control risk drove a roughly 20% weekly drop despite strong quarterly results.
Anthropic fell over 25% from its day-one high to $83.10 on day two, with full greenshoe exercised and no stabilization bid.
Amazon will own 14.7% of Anthropic post-IPO, about $206B at a $1.4T valuation, though shares are under pressure.
Reported 39% revenue growth to $3.45B and raised full-year revenue guidance to as much as $14.57B, citing threats as a demand driver.
Rose 12.1% on a day the S&P 500 fell as cybersecurity demand outlook improved.
Rose 8% on a day the S&P 500 fell on the cybersecurity demand theme.

sector_views.rationale: Worst-hit sector on the week, now underperforming the S&P 500 over the last year with heavy hedge fund selling.
Held up best on the week though staples still ended lower.
Minimal AI beta may attract diversification flows.
AI-driven threats now seen as a demand driver, with PANW, OKTA and CRWD rallying.

earnings_insights: Palo Alto Networks reported revenue growth of 39% to $3.45B and raised its full-year revenue forecast to as much as $14.57B.
Nvidia posted strong quarterly results but the stock fell anyway on AI-investment concerns, leadership uncertainty and the SEC probe. Interim CEO Kress said Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Data keep beating expectations, near the July 2023 peak of 79.6, supporting the hawkish Fed backdrop.
A sharp drop lowered odds of a 50bp December hike.
Easing long-run expectations reduce hike pressure.
Rally on growth fears despite hawkish Fed talk.
Market-implied odds were cut after Friday's equity selloff.
Lowest since August despite Hormuz attacks as supply surplus emerges.
Down from $65.56 on Oct 9, which implies lower pump prices and CPI relief.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell seven straight weeks after a Sunday liquidation cascade, erasing its post-August rally and reaching its lowest since Sept 2024.
BTC is down 54% from its October 2025 peak over 410 days, its biggest correction since 2022 and tied for the longest peak-to-trough ever.
Tradr launches 2x long and 2x short Anthropic ETFs (ANTT, ANTZ) on Monday.
risk_factors: Further Fed tightening, with Waller advocating more than reversing last year's cuts.
AI capex cut by a hyperscaler, financing strain, and heavy IPO supply.
Nvidia SEC probe, export controls and CEO vacancy.
Leveraged fund liquidation, including Situational Awareness.
Middle East shipping disruption and cyber incidents.
charts_described: Chart of the week: Nasdaq 100 down 19.8% from its peak, needing about a 25% rally to regain it.
Citi US Economic Surprise Index at 74.0 versus the July 2023 peak of 79.6.
vol_and_positioning: VIX reached 38, the highest close since Liberation Day, and Fear & Greed is at Extreme fear.
HY spreads are considerably tighter than VIX would imply.
Hedge funds dumped tech at the fastest six-week pace in at least a decade.
Average SPX return dispersion is at a level seen only twice in 40 years, in the dot-com bust and the GFC.
Druckenmiller reportedly short copper and CTAs dumping, driving metals lower.
BofA FMS: 52% expect a hyperscaler capex cut in the next 6 months, up from 30%.
geopolitical: Iran reported six tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz and drone attacks on a US air defense site in Bahrain.
US struck IRGC missile sites on Qeshm Island, and Houthis hit the Saudi PIF headquarters in Riyadh.
Trump-Xi-Putin summit in Shenzhen pledged to increase refined product supply.
Washington restricted shipments of advanced Nvidia chips to China, and the administration is set to name Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic as AI national champions per WSJ.
Cyber incidents: NSA classified network outage, Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan customer data leak claimed by group n0n, and widespread US bank outages.

Goldman forecasts a roughly 2 million barrels per day oil surplus into 2027.
Morgan Stanley expects two additional Fed hikes and sees the AI cycle continuing.

tension_points.bull_case: Morgan Stanley sees AI spend with room to run and earnings benefits spreading in 2027, with ACWI at about 15x forward earnings. GPU rental prices are up 55% YoY.
tension_points.bear_case: 52% of FMS investors expect a hyperscaler capex cut, AI stocks are red YTD, and hedge funds are selling tech at a record pace.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hyperscaler announcing a capex cut, or sticky inflation forcing more than two additional Fed hikes.
